But the check is `chunk = stream.readline(limit)`: if the line is longer than `limit`, readline returns exactly `limit` bytes without a newline → then `nxt = stream.readline(1)` returns the next byte (not empty) → overlong ✓.

What if the line is exactly limit bytes with no newline at EOF? readline(limit) returns limit bytes without a newline → then readline(1) returns b"" → we yield (chunk, False) → the line is exactly 4 MiB ✓ valid length → parsed normally ✓.

import json, random, subprocess, sys, time
import genmax
rng=random.Random(99)
reqs=[genmax.gen_request(rng,"easy") for _ in range(64)]
data=("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in reqs)+"\n").encode()
print("input size %.1f MiB" % (len(data)/1048576))
t0=time.time()
p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"/app/submission/planner.py"],input=data,capture_output=True,timeout=600)
dt=time.time()-t0

if p.stderr: print("stderr:",p.stderr.decode()[-1000:])
# interactive check
proc=subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,"/app/submission/planner.py"],stdin=subprocess.PIPE,stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
req=json.dumps(reqs[0])
t0=time.time()
proc.stdin.write((req+"\n").encode()); proc.stdin.flush()
line=proc.stdout.readline()
print("interactive first response in %.3fs:"%(time.time()-t0), line[:100].decode())
proc.stdin.write((json.dumps(reqs[1])+"\n").encode()); proc.stdin.flush()
line=proc.stdout.readline()
print("interactive second response:", line[:100].decode())
proc.stdin.close(); proc.wait()
